Replay

Framework-first completion and experimental release assessment

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Final requirement auditFinal failure-policy checkAdoption rationaleFollow-up boundaries

Assessment date: 2026-09-20. This evaluates the user's revised priority: finish the framework and use games as representative validation, while deferring exhaustive game parity. It does not retroactively declare every historical M0–M9 port/deployment checkbox complete.

Decision: retain and deliver Replay as an experimental library alongside Kit. The requested multiplayer styles have implemented primitives and representative acceptance. At this assessment, the framework completion requirements were satisfied within the explicit supported configurations. Neither human productivity superiority nor universal production/platform readiness is claimed. No release was published.

Final requirement audit#

User-facing requirement Authoritative evidence inspected Conclusion
A separate Odin/Godot library with a coherent gameplay foundation replay value timeline/pool/RNG/correction APIs; engine-free Loot; Hello models and Session adapter Implemented. Mutable gameplay dependencies are explicit; rendering and I/O remain outside simulation.
Offline, co-op, competitive authority and deterministic peer rollback Current net/group/interest/owned/P2P tests; representative Hello, Cavecrawl/Slopball, Quickdraw/Claimball and Duel integrations Implemented under separate explicit policies. No false claim of deterministic Godot contact physics or unrestricted concurrent writers.
Framework-owned difficult networking work Scheduling/action ledgers, prediction/correction, snapshots/deltas, recipient views, journals, bounded transport/routing, Party/Room/P2P setup Implemented and documented. Applications still choose game rules, trust and prediction scope.
Host migration and recovery Complete checkpoint/identity/action state; coordinator fencing; planned/crash/repeat/partition/successor-loss/return/cold-restore evidence Implemented for the tested contracts. Crash recovery may lose work after the accepted checkpoint; external exactly-once side effects are not promised.
Native/browser integration and reconnect identity Current authenticated native two-player ENet, browser RTC, durable enrollment and process-generation tests; forwarded-port creator return Implemented. Native and browser backends must match for cross-platform gameplay; validated combinations are listed in support.md.
Practical authoring/debugging Input capture and detached presentation; diagnostics/recordings/playback; checked API recipes; paid-revive/weapon authoring comparisons Implemented with structural and runtime evidence. Human authoring speed/play-feel superiority remains unproven.
Preserve both implementations and separately runnable games, including sibling Scrapyard Kit baseline hashes, clean original game paths, clean sibling revision; distinct Replay projects and isolated test profiles Preserved. Remaining full-game parity is deferred by user direction, not claimed complete.
Comparison and stabilization Current 13-gate framework smoke (400 unit tests plus recipe/target/archive checks), observer trace, protocol/fixture fixes and prior representative cost measurements Verified selection passes. The historical C2 failure's cause remains unestablished; no failing current trace or invented fix is claimed.
Deliver usable library entry points Getting-started guide, compatibility policy, checked lifecycle recipes, supported-configuration assessment and existing addon packaging Delivered in the workspace. Actual package installs/builds/runs outside the source checkout; no deployment or publication performed.

The implementation audit provides source/test mappings. Framework delivery receipts cover the smoke, recipes and forwarded endpoint case. The final assessment's receipts cover actual control service loss and a freshly built isolated consumer addon.

Final failure-policy check#

The native P2P service is killed after both encrypted links are admitted. Party readiness fails after about 10.46 seconds, and neither party claims readiness for new admissions. Existing authenticated links remain at generation 1 and both games continue to the full-reference tick-1200 hash 9004447930841423017.

The observed behavior is explicit: existing P2P gameplay can survive background control loss, but new admission cannot. Automatic control reconnection is not implemented by the current Party owner. The application may close/reopen and restore/rejoin after service recovery. Signed denial/invalidity has a different policy and clears native link keys. The documented policy requires an application decision after control loss; it does not retry indefinitely or promise recovery from every outage.

Adoption rationale#

Replay makes cross-entity operations ordinary value-world code, with shared replay and authority execution. The paid-revive comparison demonstrates that property for one real feature. It does not prove every feature is easier. Runtime costs in representative comparisons are often higher than Kit's; measured compression improvements do not remove the CPU/copying tradeoff. The result supports keeping Replay available for experiments and game-specific evaluation, rather than replacing Kit automatically. Both game versions remain useful for that evaluation.

Follow-up boundaries#

The following work remains outside the completed framework-first scope: exhaustive game content/visual/audio parity; human comparative playtests; broader independent OS/hardware/browser validation; live Steam/GameServer and public account/deployment operations; arbitrary NAT and outage combinations; independent cryptographic review; automatic failed-control reconnection; and storage/prediction extensions beyond the documented bounded model.

They are not being represented as finished. Advertising any of them as validated requires new evidence. The original detailed roadmap and historical results remain available for future work. The delivered experimental framework should be pinned to a source/toolchain revision and used according to its compatibility policy.
